# #702 — CI flake: same SHA passes on push, fails 6 tests on pull_request (exit 127 in deploy ref-gate, ENOENT in spool)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-09T17:40:05Z
Updated: 2026-08-09T17:40:05Z

---

Two `check` jobs ran the **same commit** `f0e135c90a5d327db2fb229098272dfe3fb83682` (PR #701) and disagreed:

| workflow event | run | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `push` | [31326750319](https://github.com/rodaddy/open-brain/actions/runs/31326750319) | SUCCESS |
| `pull_request` | [31326759896](https://github.com/rodaddy/open-brain/actions/runs/31326759896) | FAILURE — 6 tests |

Identical tree, opposite verdicts. Per `docs/lane-contract.md` (rounds 17/20), the two-runs-same-SHA comparison is the flake signal, so this is filed rather than absorbed or retried into green.

## The 6 failures, two clusters

**Cluster 1 — `scripts/core01-deploy-local.integration.test.ts` (5 tests)**

```
Expected: 1
Received: 127
  at expectGateRefusal (scripts/core01-deploy-local.integration.test.ts:236:27)
```

- lets a current-main manual dispatch reach only host preflight
- lets a reachable version tag reach only host preflight
- refuses a stale manual commit before env loading or staging
- refuses a tag outside main ancestry before env loading or staging
- refuses unsupported provider and event metadata before preflight

**Exit 127 is the shell's "command not found."** The test expects the deploy script's gate to refuse with exit 1; instead the script itself never ran. That is a missing binary / PATH difference on the runner, not a wrong refusal — and it means these five assertions were not testing the gate on that run at all.

**Cluster 2 — `clients/ts/tests/spool.test.ts` (1 test)**

```
(fail) JsonlSpool durability and cross-process exclusion >
       preserves every acknowledged key from independently opened child spools
code: "ENOENT"
```

Every other test in the same describe block passed, including the neighbouring durability and lock-recovery cases. A lone `ENOENT` in a spool test that spawns child processes points at a filesystem/temp-dir difference between the two runners.

## Evidence these are environment-owned, not tree-owned

Both clusters pass locally on **both** trees, in separate worktrees:

- clean `origin/main` @ 123cc63, fresh worktree: **29 pass / 0 fail** (exit 0)
- PR #701 branch @ f0e135c: **29 pass / 0 fail** (exit 0)

Neither test file is in #701's diff, which touches only `src/tools/__tests__/get-contract.test.ts`, `scripts/done-means/271-tripwire-acknowledges-contract-moves.sh`, `scripts/done-means/sme-per-entry-files.sh`, and two `docs/sme/` files.

## Not to be confused with the main-red item #701 fixes

`main` @ 123cc63's own CI run fails on a *different* test — `get_contract > advertises hot memory only through the agent_context_pack pull boundary (#271)` — which is a real, deterministic tree defect and is exactly what PR #701 heals. On #701 that test passes in CI. The 6 failures above are separate and are the subject of this issue.

## Suggested next step

Compare the two runners' environments for the `check` job (PATH and available shell tooling for cluster 1, temp-dir/permissions for cluster 2). Exit 127 should ideally not be able to masquerade as a gate verdict: `expectGateRefusal` asserting `toBe(1)` treats "script did not run" and "script refused" as distinguishable only by luck of the number, so a guard there (fail loudly on 127) would turn this class of flake into a legible error.
